summary: Defines a conference event package for tightly coupled conferences using the SIP events framework, with the data format for notifications. Users can subscribe to a conference URI and are notified of changes such as who joined or left. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: You can ask a meeting room to tell you whenever someone comes in or leaves. This sets up that message service for internet conference calls.

questions: who is in a sip conference
what is the sip conference event package
how to subscribe to a sip conference
subtitle: How a SIP client can subscribe to a conference and be told who joins, who leaves and what changes.

tldr.problem: People in a SIP conference, and tools that manage one, need a standard way to learn who is in the conference, what media is flowing and when something changes.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4575 defines a SIP event package named conference. A subscriber sends SUBSCRIBE to the conference URI, and the focus replies with NOTIFY messages carrying an XML conference information document, usually only the parts that changed.
tldr.outcome: Subscribers rebuild the full picture of the conference by merging full and partial documents in version order. The RFC stresses that this information is sensitive, so subscriptions should be authenticated and authorized.

facts.label: Recommended notification rate
facts.value: no faster than once every 5 seconds per subscriber

today: RFC 4575 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata for this site lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It remains the definition of the SIP conference event package.

sections.title: A Package for Conference State
sections.content:
The SIP events framework (RFC 3265) lets a client subscribe to events and receive notifications. It introduces the package: one specific use of the framework for a well-defined set of events. RFC 4575 defines a package for tightly coupled conferences.

In the SIP conferencing framework (RFC 4353), subscriptions to a conference URI are routed to the focus that handles the conference. The focus acts as the notifier and sends clients updates on conference state: the conference identifiers, the participants (optionally with their status and media), sidebars and service URIs.
sections.eli5: A conference has a host who always knows what is going on. This RFC lets you sign up to get updates from that host.

sections.title: How the Conference Package Works
sections.content:
The package name is conference, carried in the Event and Allow-Events headers. A conference is a URI that identifies a SIP user agent called the focus, which makes sure everyone in the conference can communicate. The focus knows enough about the conference to inform subscribers. If a participant is itself another focus, the first focus MAY subscribe to that focus too and report the cascaded participants using the <cascaded-focus> element.

A SUBSCRIBE with no body means the default filtering policy: a notification for every change in conference state, normally carrying only what changed. The exception is the NOTIFY sent in response to a SUBSCRIBE, which carries the full state. The RFC does not define filters. The default subscription lasts one hour, and when the conference ends all subscriptions are terminated with the reason noresource.

The NOTIFY body is a conference information document in the application/conference-info+xml format. All subscribers and notifiers MUST support it, and it is the default if no Accept header was sent. If an Accept header is present it MUST include that type.

  • Notifications SHOULD be sent when a participant joins or leaves.
  • Changes in participant status, media or other optional information MAY be reported, subject to local policy.
  • Changes in conference identifiers and service URIs SHOULD be reported to subscribers.
  • It is RECOMMENDED that a server sends no more than one notification per subscriber every 5 seconds.

Conferences are centralized, so SUBSCRIBE requests should not generally fork. If forking happens, a subscriber MUST NOT establish more than one SIP dialog from a single SUBSCRIBE. Cascaded foci MAY act as state agents.
sections.eli5: You sign up once, get a full list first, and after that you only hear about changes. The host will not text you more than once every few seconds, so your phone is not flooded.

sections.title: Full, Partial and Deleted Documents
sections.content:
The conference document is XML that MUST be well-formed and valid, based on XML 1.0 and encoded in UTF-8. Its namespace is urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:conference-info. The root element <conference-info> MUST carry a version attribute, the only meaningful version number for the whole document.

To save bandwidth, the package uses partial notifications. Elements that carry a lot of data that changes often (<conference-info>, <users>, <user>, <endpoint>, <sidebars-by-val> and <sidebars-by-ref>) have a state attribute with the value full, partial or deleted. The default is full. A child's state MUST be consistent with its parent's: if the parent is full, so are its children. All subscribing clients MUST support this mechanism. To let updates target one item, each repeatable element has a key: entity for <user> and <endpoint>, id for <media>.

The subscriber keeps a local version number and a local copy of each element, and follows this procedure:

  1. The first full document sets the local version and the local data.
  2. A document whose version is equal to or lower than the local version is discarded.
  3. A full or deleted document replaces the local data. Deleted on the root means the conference has ceased to exist, and the subscriber SHOULD end the subscription with SUBSCRIBE and Expires = 0.
  4. A partial document whose version is more than one above the local version means a notification was missed, so the subscriber MUST send a subscription refresh to trigger a full-state notification.
  5. If the version is exactly one higher, the subscriber merges it: new keys add rows, existing keys are updated, and elements marked deleted are removed.

The server MUST increment the 32-bit version number for each notification that reports a change, and for each partial notification it increases by one.
sections.eli5: Each update has a number. If the number is lower than what you have, ignore it. If it skips ahead, you missed one, so ask for the whole list again. Otherwise, just fix the parts that changed.

sections.title: The Conference Information Document
sections.content:
The format describes the conference and who takes part. Conferences contain users, a user can have multiple endpoints, and each endpoint can have multiple media streams. Conferences can also include or reference sidebar conferences. The RFC does not say how the focus learns this information: it may come from call signaling or from an administrator, subject to local policy.

The <conference-info> root has an entity (the conference URI to SUBSCRIBE to), a state and a version. Its children are <conference-description>, <host-info>, <conference-state>, <users>, <sidebars-by-ref> and <sidebars-by-val>. A full document MUST at least include <conference-description> and <users>.

  • Description: subject, free text, keywords, <conf-uris> for ways to join (with a purpose of participation or streaming), <service-uris> (web-page, recording, event), <maximum-user-count> as a hint, and <available-media>.
  • Conference state: <user-count>, which may exceed the number of listed users, <active>, and <locked>, meaning no one can be added to the roster.
  • Users: each <user> has a unique entity URI. If the focus hides a participant's identity, the host part MUST use the .invalid top-level domain, for example sip:anonymousX@anonymous.invalid.
  • Endpoints and media: an <endpoint> describes a device or signaling session, with status, how it joined and left, its media streams and optional SIP dialog identifiers in <call-info>. Each <media> has a <type>, a <label> and a <status> such as sendrecv or recvonly. <src-id> can carry an RTP SSRC so participants can map a speaker to a user.
  • Sidebars: sub-conferences listed by reference (<sidebars-by-ref>) or described inline (<sidebars-by-val>).
sections.eli5: The update is like a seating chart for the meeting. It lists the room, the people, the devices each person uses, and what each device is sending, such as sound or video.

sections.title: Endpoint Status and How Endpoints Join or Leave
sections.content:
Each endpoint has a <status> that tells subscribers where it is in the conference. Some are transient, such as alerting and disconnecting, and could generate a lot of traffic. Implementations MAY therefore notify only certain participants about them, or not at all.

The <joining-method> is dialed-in, dialed-out or focus-owner. The <disconnection-method> is departed, booted, failed or busy. Both come with optional info elements holding a UTC time (when), a reason (the format of RFC 3326 is RECOMMENDED) and a by URI saying who caused it.
sections.eli5: Each person's device has a label like "waiting at the door", "inside and talking" or "muted". There are also notes on how they came in and how they left.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
Conference state can reveal very sensitive information. The RFC RECOMMENDS strong authentication, protection of conference information and comprehensive authorization rules. It also says that all subscriptions SHOULD be authenticated and then authorized, though it RECOMMENDS letting every user in the conference subscribe.

  • A focus is RECOMMENDED to authenticate subscribers with normal SIP mechanisms such as Digest.
  • The transport of the information MUST ensure integrity and SHOULD ensure confidentiality, using end-to-end encryption such as S/MIME. Without that, a focus is RECOMMENDED to use mutual hop-by-hop TLS.
  • A notification server MUST be able to generate different views of the conference for different subscribers, based on role and access rights.
  • A focus MUST support requests for privacy, indicated by conference policy or by the SIP Privacy header field. For such a participant, no identity SHOULD be revealed in any URI, and the anonymous URI convention MUST be followed.
sections.eli5: Knowing who is in a meeting can be private. So the host should check who you are before telling you, and should hide names of people who ask not to be named.

sections.title: What the RFC Registers
sections.content: The RFC registers the event package conference, the MIME type application/conference-info+xml, the XML namespace urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:conference-info and an XML schema. It also creates a new sub-registry called URI purposes under the existing SIP parameters registry. The initial values are participation, streaming, event, recording and web-page. New values are registered by IANA under a specification-required policy.
sections.eli5: It adds the new service's name and file type to the official lists, so everyone uses the same words.

viz.caption: OVERALL HIERARCHY OF THE DOCUMENT (RFC 4575, SECTION 5.1)

items.label: Connected
items.desc: A participant in the conference; can send and receive media depending on policy.

items.label: Disconnected
items.desc: Not a participant, and no active dialog with the focus.

items.label: On hold
items.desc: Dialog exists but the endpoint neither hears nor is mixed into the conference.

items.label: Muted via focus
items.desc: Can listen, but its media is not mixed in.

items.label: Pending
items.desc: Not yet in the session but expected to join soon.

items.label: Alerting
items.desc: PSTN ALERTING or SIP 180 Ringing was returned for the outbound call.

items.label: Dialing in
items.desc: Dialing in, not yet in the roster.

items.label: Dialing out
items.desc: Focus has dialed out, endpoint not yet in the roster.

items.label: Disconnecting
items.desc: Focus is disconnecting the endpoint, for example by sending BYE.
